item.title: UTSA vs. UAB: 5 players to watch as Roadrunners defense looks to stay hot
item.description: UTSA Roadrunners linebacker Bryce Grays (26) yells out during a game against the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley, at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) Scouring offensive film this week, UTSA coach Jeff Traylor is on the lookout for signs that he's giving something up. Whether it was a signal, a specific player's stance or some other culprit, Traylor felt like the offense was "always one play behind" in Saturday's 35-16 win against North Texas. Traylor worries the Roadrunners are somehow tipping plays, as the Mean Green often seemed to know what was coming next. With a struggling offensive line and a shift to a more conservative approach to protect a lead, UTSA came up empty on its first four drives of the second half, totaling just 30 yards. A'Marion Peterson's 179 rushing yards and single-game UTSA record four touchdowns on just 11 carries helped mask the issues for the Roadrunners, who finished with 326 total yards. "Extremely frustrated right now with our offensive performance. We were given too many chances," Traylor said. "The game should have been over. It really should have been. We've got to look at what that is." With North Texas battling injuries to its top two stars in quarterback Tayven Jackson and running back Jahiem White, Traylor knew Mean Green coach Neal Brown was mostly handcuffed. UTSA's defense was also playing its best game of the season, and Traylor said he figured "we would have to lose the game offensively, was the only way for us to lose." "That's bad ball on my part, probably," Traylor said, "but I just had that much faith in our defense, and I knew Neal was in trouble with his personnel over there." Five defensive standouts who could be in focus again if UTSA hits another offensive rut during a road matchup against UAB at 7 p.m. Saturday: Bryce Grays, linebacker UTSA Roadrunners' Bryce Grays defends against South Florida's Joshua Porter in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) After watching how Grays "really took a step" and was "noticeably different" against North Texas, Traylor joked that the senior linebacker better go back to the same pregame meal next week. Grays said the routine didn't stray far from the norm - a spinach smoothie, and an omelet with spinach, tomatoes, sausage and bacon. "I had some potatoes, so maybe the carbs," Grays said with a smile. "I don't know, but I'll definitely have it again this week." Grays notched a career-high seven tackles, adding 1.5 tackles for loss and half of a sack. Traylor described it as "the best I've ever seen Bryce play," as the senior showed more violence in his tackling. Grays said last year's game against North Texas, when he finished without a tackle across 17 snaps of a 55-17 loss, was another motivator on Saturday. item.content:encoded: UTSA Roadrunners linebacker Bryce Grays (26) yells out during a game against the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley, at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) Scouring offensive film this week, UTSA coach Jeff Traylor is on the lookout for signs that he's giving something up. Whether it was a signal, a specific player's stance or some other culprit, Traylor felt like the offense was "always one play behind" in Saturday's 35-16 win against North Texas. Traylor worries the Roadrunners are somehow tipping plays, as the Mean Green often seemed to know what was coming next. With a struggling offensive line and a shift to a more conservative approach to protect a lead, UTSA came up empty on its first four drives of the second half, totaling just 30 yards. A'Marion Peterson's 179 rushing yards and single-game UTSA record four touchdowns on just 11 carries helped mask the issues for the Roadrunners, who finished with 326 total yards. "Extremely frustrated right now with our offensive performance. We were given too many chances," Traylor said. "The game should have been over. It really should have been. We've got to look at what that is." With North Texas battling injuries to its top two stars in quarterback Tayven Jackson and running back Jahiem White, Traylor knew Mean Green coach Neal Brown was mostly handcuffed. UTSA's defense was also playing its best game of the season, and Traylor said he figured "we would have to lose the game offensively, was the only way for us to lose." "That's bad ball on my part, probably," Traylor said, "but I just had that much faith in our defense, and I knew Neal was in trouble with his personnel over there." Five defensive standouts who could be in focus again if UTSA hits another offensive rut during a road matchup against UAB at 7 p.m. Saturday: Bryce Grays, linebacker UTSA Roadrunners' Bryce Grays defends against South Florida's Joshua Porter in a game against South Florida at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) After watching how Grays "really took a step" and was "noticeably different" against North Texas, Traylor joked that the senior linebacker better go back to the same pregame meal next week. Grays said the routine didn't stray far from the norm - a spinach smoothie, and an omelet with spinach, tomatoes, sausage and bacon. "I had some potatoes, so maybe the carbs," Grays said with a smile. "I don't know, but I'll definitely have it again this week." Grays notched a career-high seven tackles, adding 1.5 tackles for loss and half of a sack. Traylor described it as "the best I've ever seen Bryce play," as the senior showed more violence in his tackling. Grays said last year's game against North Texas, when he finished without a tackle across 17 snaps of a 55-17 loss, was another motivator on Saturday. "I was putting my body on the line for my teammates. I love those guys, and I'd do anything for them. So, it was a game of high emotions," Grays said. "It was just a whole lot going on. So, I just wanted to be the best that I could for my teammates." Jusiah Sampleton, defensive lineman UTSA Roadrunners defensive lineman Jusiah Sampleton (91) reacts after a fumble recovery during the first quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) After UTSA gave up 339 rushing yards in a 60-29 loss at FAU two weeks ago, Traylor challenged the Roadrunners to find their physicality again, feeling the group had been outworked in the trenches. The 6-foot, 315-pound Sampleton anchored that effort in the middle, making his fourth start of the season as UTSA held North Texas to 109 rushing yards at an average of 2.7 yards per carry. "That was the challenge of the whole week, just because we reestablished the line of scrimmage," Traylor said. "There's just a ton of video evidence where we played on their side of the line, where if you go back and watch the week before, that did not happen. ... It was a mindset all week." Brandon Tucker, inside linebacker UTSA Roadrunners linebacker Brandon Tucker (23) prepares for the snap during the first quarter against the Colorado State Rams in San Antonio, Texas, Saturday, Sept., 26, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Returning after a one-week absence due to injury, Tucker notched five tackles against North Texas and made a leaping stab to break up a pass in the end zone, nearly securing an interception. "It's not a coincidence we played a lot better with B Tuck showing back up in the lineup," Traylor said. "It's just his spirit, his leadership, his experience, physicality. Great football player. Glad to get him back." Owen Pewee, linebacker UTSA Roadrunners linebacker Owen Pewee (2) makes a tackle during the third quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) Reviewing some of UTSA's highlights in a team meeting this week, Traylor pointed out how much ground Pewee covered on the way to a forced fumble during Saturday's second quarter. Pewee was about 15 yards behind the play when North Texas' Baron Tipton caught a ball up the seam, but Pewee tracked him down and punched the ball loose from behind, giving UTSA possession. "Just his typical self," Traylor said, "unbelievable effort." Pewee also notched seven tackles, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hurry in the game, continuing to show his versatility as the Roadrunners slide him between pass-rusher, slot corner and inside linebacker. Elijah Baldwin, linebacker UTSA Roadrunners outside linebacker Elijah Baldwin (32) reacts after making a tackle during the fourth quarter against the Rice Owls in Houston, Texas, Saturday, Oct., 3, 2026. (Zach Del Bello/San Antonio Express-News) The UTEP transfer and San Antonio native delivered his most productive game, converting his first 1.5 sacks of the season. Though Traylor acknowledged that the stats draw the most attention, he said Baldwin has "played well all year" for the Roadrunners, "working his tail off" since his arrival. Fellow edge rusher Cam Cooper also had a sack Saturday to give him two this season, showing signs of progress at a position that has struggled in 2026. The Roadrunners still rank No. 119 in the FBS with 1.3 sacks per game. "We've been hurting there this year. We have not gotten home as much as we wanted to at that spot," Traylor said. "Those guys have been a little frustrated. I think this gives the room some confidence." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Sharpe Tells Patriots Fans: A.J. Brown Brought His Own Failure
item.description: Football - NFL - Detroit Lions v New England Patriots - Allianz Arena, Munich, Germany - November 15, 2026 Detroit Lions' Jared Goff is sacked by New England Patriots' Milton Williams REUTERS/Angelika Warmuth The New England Patriots are in a deep hole after a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday in Munich. The team sits at 5-5, but the bigger issue is the complete failure of their biggest offseason acquisition. A.J. Brown has missed six games, caught just 11 passes for 128 yards, and scored zero touchdowns. This is not bad luck. It is a direct result of behavior that Shannon Sharpe says the receiver created all by himself. Sharpe did not hold back during his appearance on the Nightcap podcast. He pointed out that Brown complained constantly while with the Philadelphia Eagles, even though they were winning games. “Nobody’s feeling sorry for A.J. because he brought this on himself,” Sharpe said, according to MARCA . The former NFL star noted that Brown b*tched and moped about his role despite going to the Super Bowl. Now that he is in New England, the situation is worse, and the public sympathy is gone. Sharpe added that Brown should have supported his quarterback instead of attacking him. “So why would you do that to the brother quarterback?” Sharpe added. A Expensive Mistake The financial stakes for this failure are massive. To acquire Brown, the Patriots surrendered a 2028 first-round pick alongside a 2027 fifth-round selection. He is earning $29 million this season on a contract that includes $84 million in guaranteed money. Former Tennessee Titans general manager Ran Carthon believes the team cannot afford to wait any longer. Carthon told NFL on CBS that New England needs to act fast. “You don’t want to compound a mistake by holding on to it too long. You cut your losses,” Carthon said. Even if they move on, the Patriots will take a $25.9 million dead cap hit. That is a heavy price to pay for a player who has been injured and unproductive. The trade looked bad before the season, but it looks like a disaster now. Brown has struggled with drops and has failed to get separation against defenders. Old Friends Turn Critical Even Patriots legend Rob Gronkowski is calling this a disappointment. Gronk appeared on “The Gronk & Jules Show” and admitted he does not want to say how bad things are. “I don’t even wanna say it because he’s been such a great player, but it’s been a disappointment,” Gronkowski said, according to Pro Football Network . He wants to see Brown’s engine start, but the results so far are not there. Boomer Esiason was even harsher, calling Brown an “unmitigated disaster” since arriving in Foxborough. Esiason also questioned whether Brown wanted to play after leaving the game with another hamstring injury. The Patriots have seven games left in the regular season. item.title: McCaffrey’s Historic Night Exposes Dallas Defensive Woes
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys defense fell apart in a way that feels impossible to fix after Sunday night. San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey put on a show that will haunt this team for a long time. He became the first player ever to hit specific rushing and receiving marks in one game while his team won 46-40. The 49ers offense racked up 584 yards in the game against the Dallas Cowboys, a number that simply does not happen often. McCaffrey did everything he could to win the game. With 13 carries, he gained 62 yards and scored a touchdown. Four catches yielded a team-leading 161 yards and two touchdowns for him. The record he set is the kind that stands for decades. The Cowboys defense could not stop the opponent’s skill and opportunity. The Record-Breaking Finish The game felt like a blowout in the second half. With 2:26 remaining in the first half, Purdy threw a 74-yard touchdown pass to McCaffrey according to a report . He did not stop there. He caught a 60-yard touchdown with 3:23 left in the final quarter. To give San Francisco a 14-point lead, he caught the two-point conversion. The plays resulted from a player who has been dominant all year. After nine games, McCaffrey has recorded 115 carries, 519 yards, and 10 touchdowns. Dallas fans expected a fight, but they got a master class. The 49ers offense moved the ball at will, and the Cowboys had no answer. This was a night where the stats tell the whole story without any extra words needed. The numbers show exactly how far the defense fell short. Nine games have seen McCaffrey averaging 4.5 yards per carry. He has three touchdowns, 431 yards and 40 catches. A Legacy Built on Yards This performance adds to a career that is already full of records. Already this season, McCaffrey is putting up nearly 1,000 yards from scrimmage. With 3,864, he set the NCAA record for all-purpose yards, a record that still stands today. Behind Derrick Henry, he finished as the Heisman Trophy runner-up. He holds the record with 6,987 career all-purpose yards.

item.title: Aaron Kramer Takes Helm As Dodge’s NASCAR Crew Chief For 2027
item.description: David Leong-Imagn Images Kaulig Racing has named Aaron Kramer as the crew chief for Ty Dillon, marking the first key hire for Dodge’s return to the Cup Series in 2027. The 38-year-old from Wellsville, New York, moves from Haas Factory Team where he served as Cole Custer’s crew chief through the 2025 and 2026 seasons. This move sets the stage for a major rebuild of the No. 10 car as the manufacturer comes back after a long absence. The Engineering Background Kramer brings a specific skill set that Kaulig Racing CEO Chris Rice says is exactly what the team needs right now. Before his time at Haas, Kramer spent several seasons with RFK Racing in engineering roles where he worked as Chris Buescher’s lead race engineer. He was part of the group when Buescher won five Cup Series races between 2022 and 2024. Rice noted in a prepared statement that “Aaron has the exact engineering mindset and practical background we need as we lay the groundwork for 2027.” The CEO also pointed out that Kramer worked with Ryan Newman during his career. A graduate of UNC-Charlotte with a degree in mechanical engineering, Kramer started his NASCAR career in 2010. His resume covers car preparation, vehicle performance, and race engineering, not just calling races from the pit box. Kramer called the new role “a great opportunity” because Kaulig is at a “big turning point for the team.” He added that building a Cup program from the ground up with a returning manufacturer like Dodge takes “a ton of focus, solid engineering and relentless preparation.” Testing the New Machines Dillon and his teammate, veteran A.J. Allmendinger, are already leading the on-track testing and development for Kaulig’s No. 10 and No. 16 Dodges. This is not the first time Kaulig has faced a huge development task in recent years. After a 13-year absence, the original equipment manufacturer returned to NASCAR competition in 2026 when the team fielded five Ram trucks in the Craftsman Truck Series. That experience in the truck series gave the team a head start on managing a new manufacturer relationship. The pressure is on to get the cars ready for the 2027 season, and having a crew chief with deep engineering roots helps. Fans and teams alike know that a new manufacturer needs more than just speed; they need a team that understands how the cars are built. Kramer’s background suggests he can handle the technical side while managing the driver and the pit crew. A Fresh Start for Dodge Dodge’s return to the sport is a big deal for the industry, and this hire signals a serious commitment to winning. The team is adding a car and building a program from the ground up with a specific plan. As per AOL.com , the focus is on laying the groundwork for a full Cup Series run next year. The success of this venture will depend on how well the engineering team works with the drivers on the track. With the offseason underway, the team will continue to refine the cars before the first race of the new season. Dillon and All

item.title: LeBron James Denies Patience Request To Sixers Coaches
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY LeBron James shut down rumors with a direct and forceful denial on Monday. The 41-year-old forward took to Instagram to reject an ESPN report claiming he asked the Philadelphia 76ers coaching staff to be patient with his injury management. James stated clearly, “Those words never came out of my mouth!” The report from Dave McMenamin suggested James wanted the team to wait on his return, but the player says that story is simply wrong. Philly fans know James has been dealing with back issues all season. He has missed games on and off due to sciatica in his back, according to HITC. His stats show he is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 6.9 assists this year. He is also using the ball less and playing at a slower pace than ever before. Record-Breaking Passing Game While the denial made headlines, James also hit a massive career milestone on the court. During a matchup against the Indiana Pacers, he moved to No. 3 on the NBA’s assist leaderboard. He now has 12,092 assists, which puts him behind only Chris Paul and John Stockton. He is helping the team win games even when he is not scoring at his usual high rate. James spoke to reporters after reaching that number with genuine humility. “I mean, obviously it’s super humbling,” he told the media. He added, “It’s something that I didn’t obviously foresee in my career, but I knew assists meant a lot to me.”

item.title: Last-gasp Haaland shoots Norway into Nations League quarters
item.description: Pedro Neto was among the goals for Portugal in Cardiff (Paul ELLIS) Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback from two goals down to win 3-2. Manchester City striker Haaland stroked home from the spot in the sixth minute of injury time in Copenhagen as Norway leapfrogged their hosts into second place in Group A, on head-to-head record as both teams finished on nine points. Both teams ended the group stage six points behind winners Portugal, who got their first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a 3-2 success against Wales. The winner was one of two goals from Haaland, who also started the fightback in the 37th minute -- and had a goal disallowed -- after early strikes from Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a commanding lead in front of passionate support. Haaland was given the chance to nick a spot in the last eight from the Danes, who only needed a draw to go through, after a handball from Joachim Andersen which was spotted by the VAR officials just as the hosts thought they had survived another in a series of scares. Denmark had been on the back foot ever since Haaland halved the deficit when a howler from Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen gifted possession to Martin Odegaard. It was Odegaard who forced home Norway's leveller with six minutes remaining and set up a grandstand finish which was completed with Haaland's dramatic winner. "This has been one of the craziest years in football I've ever experienced," said a relieved Haaland to TV2 in Norway. Norway will join Portugal in Friday's draw in Nyon, where the four group winners will be seeded and each play against one of the four second-placed teams. - Portugal bounce back - Haaland's winner made Portugal's win over Wales irrelevant to their group placing, but Carlos Forbs' classy strike in the 70th minute in Cardiff made sure of a positive finish for Jorge Jesus' team. Forbs' first international goal decided a hugely entertaining encounter in which Wales, already guaranteed to finish bottom of the group, put in a performance which belied their position. Wales will take part in the play-offs to decide the final promotion and relegation spots between Leagues A and B, and on Tuesday's evidence they have a fighting chance of staying in the top tier. David Brooks quickly replied to Bruno Fernandes' superb opener for Portugal and Wales had their tails up when Sorba Thomas slid the hosts in front in the 40th minute. But Pedro Neto, who was later sent off, almost immediately levelled the scores and Forbs decided an even contest and ensured Portugal would bounce back from a humiliating defeat at the hands of Denmark at the weekend. "It's a special feeling; I won't forget today. The most important thing is that we managed to win," said Forbs. "We needed the goal to calm the game down, and it just so happened that I scored." Haaland was given the chance to nick a spot in the last eight from the Danes, who only needed a draw to go through, after a handball from Joachim Andersen which was spotted by the VAR officials just as the hosts thought they had survived another in a series of scares. Denmark had been on the back foot ever since Haaland halved the deficit when a howler from Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen gifted possession to Martin Odegaard. It was Odegaard who forced home Norway's leveller with six minutes remaining and set up a grandstand finish which was completed with Haaland's dramatic winner. "This has been one of the craziest years in football I've ever experienced," said a relieved Haaland to TV2 in Norway. Norway will join Portugal in Friday's draw in Nyon, where the four group winners will be seeded and each play against one of the four second-placed teams. - Portugal bounce back - Haaland's winner made Portugal's win over Wales irrelevant to their group placing, but Carlos Forbs' classy strike in the 70th minute in Cardiff made sure of a positive finish for Jorge Jesus' team. Forbs' first international goal decided a hugely entertaining encounter in which Wales, already guaranteed to finish bottom of the group, put in a performance which belied their position. Wales will take part in the play-offs to decide the final promotion and relegation spots between Leagues A and B, and on Tuesday's evidence they have a fighting chance of staying in the top tier. David Brooks quickly replied to Bruno Fernandes' superb opener for Portugal and Wales had their tails up when Sorba Thomas slid the hosts in front in the 40th minute. But Pedro Neto, who was later sent off, almost immediately levelled the scores and Forbs decided an even contest and ensured Portugal would bounce back from a humiliating defeat at the hands of Denmark at the weekend. "It's a special feeling; I won't forget today. The most important thing is that we managed to win," said Forbs. "We needed the goal to calm the game down, and it just so happened that I scored." Northern Ireland were promoted to League A for the first time after Justin Devenny's thumping strike gave his team the draw they needed against Hungary in Budapest. Devenny, who plays for Stoke City in England's second tier, lashed home a beautiful strike in the 65th minute at the Ferenc Puskas Arena to level the match at 1-1 and secure a second successive promotion for Michael O'Neill's team. "I feel amazing. I'm due one, that was my second for Northern Ireland. To see the game out, we dug deep and we've deserved it. We've had a great campaign and we can't wait for more," said Devenny to the BBC. Republic of Ireland will join Wales in the play-offs after closing out Group B3 with a 3-0 win over 10-man Kosovo and moving into second place. td/lp/pb

item.title: Chiefs Cut Two Receivers To Fix Broken Running Back Room
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs made a sharp move on Tuesday to shore up their offense. The team cut two wide receivers from the practice squad to make room for a tight end and a running back. Charles Goldman of A to Z Sports reported the team terminated the contracts of Jacob De Jesus and Bub Means. In a single move, the squad added TE John FitzPatrick and RB E.J. Smith. Why The Receiver Room Is Safe Letting go of De Jesus and Means feels bold, but the math makes sense. The team already added Josh Downs in a trade, so the wide receiver spot is no longer a panic point. A to Z Sports noted that Jared Wiley has a fractured ankle and will likely land on injured reserve soon. With Wiley out, the team needs bodies at tight end more than extra pass catchers. FitzPatrick brings size at 6-foot-7 and 262 pounds to fill that gap. He played college football at Georgia and won a national title there before moving to the pros. FitzPatrick played 22 games over two seasons with the Green Bay Packers. That period saw him tally nine catches, 54 yards, and a touchdown. His addition gives the Chiefs a reliable option when the starting tight end is out. Smith Returns To Fill A Void He is the son of Hall of Famer Emmitt Smith, a fact that draws plenty of attention. Smith was waived earlier in September with an injury designation but is now fully healthy. According to A to Z Sports, he trained with the team over the weekend prior to returning to the club. The Chiefs needed him because Kenneth Walker and Jaydn Ott are both dealing with injuries. Without Smith, the team would have only one backup running back for the upcoming game. That happened in Week 10 when Nate Carter was the sole backup to Emmett Johnson. Smith was also mentioned by special teams coach Dave Toub earlier this year as a player who could help on the return unit. Reid Praises The Young Roster The injury list is long, but the rookie class is stepping up to cover the gaps. Emmett Johnson ran for 101 yards and scored twice in the 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Kahlil Benson has played well in place of the injured Josh Simmons. The Associated Press quoted Chiefs coach Andy Reid on the success of these young players. “We’re one of the youngest teams in the league and they’re getting better every week,” Reid said. He added that the coaching staff must have patience with the new faces. “It’s good that the coaches keep coaching them. Got to have a little patience with them, but they’re doing a heck of a job.” The team faces the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22 at Arrowhead Stadium.

item.title: Stop Waiting For Race Day And Get The FanSided App Now
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR fans finally have a single place to get every update they need without jumping between websites. The new FanSided app arrived on Monday to replace the old way of following the sport. This free tool lets users build a custom feed with news on over 600 teams and leagues, according to Beyond The Flag . You can track drivers, see penalty updates, and follow playoff scenarios all in one spot. The launch comes right as the season slows down, giving fans time to set up their profiles before February. FanSided’s brand-new and fully customizable app has arrived, according to Beyond the Flag. NASCAR enthusiasts now have a redesigned method to track their favorite drivers and teams all year via this update. Michael Castillo covered the launch for the outlet, noting that all coverage from Beyond the Flag is now inside the app. Users get breaking news, reactions, and analysis on NASCAR’s hottest topics. The app also covers other racing series like Formula 1 and IndyCar. iPhone and Android users can download it at no cost. Build Your Own Race Day Feed By downloading the app, readers may choose coverage spanning over 600 teams, leagues, topics, and events. A personalized feed combining content from every FanSided network site results from your selections. This means you see stories on the drivers you root for and the ones you root against. Never missing a moment of the action is easier than ever thanks to the new app. You can check qualifying results or see who was penalized before the green flag without hunting for links. Stay close to Beyond the Flag wherever you are during the race. With the NASCAR offseason here, the launch timing could not be better. This is an ideal moment to download and test the app so you are fully prepared. You can set up your own personalized settings while the track is quiet. Staying informed remains valuable even in months when little seems to occur. The app finds stories for you. Get the Founding Fan Badge Before Time Runs Out iPhone and Android devices can access the FanSided app for free. Account creation is optional for app usage. Yet, creating a free account within the app before December 31 grants a limited-edition Founding Fan badge on your profile. This badge unlocks future perks for all things FanSided. Live with NASCAR, F1, and IndyCar coverage among over 600 topics, the redesigned and customizable app is now available. Beyond the Flag stories are now just one tap away for users. The new FanSided app helps fans follow daily conversations about the series, teams and drivers. You can take Beyond the Flag into race day to catch up on qualifying or confusion about how the NASCAR metric works. Need updates on stage results or point standings under NASCAR’s new “Chase” postseason format? The app keeps it all right there.

item.title: Bears Defense Has Stars But Still Can’t Stop The Run
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears defense sits at a crossroads after their bye week. On paper, the unit looks like a top-ten force in the NFL. According to Yahoo Sports , the squad holds the 11th overall spot with a 76.8 PFN Defense Impact grade following Week 10. They sit in the bottom half of the league for yards allowed per carry at 4.4. Jeffery Simmons has been a monster since arriving. He ranks second among all NFL defensive players regardless of position, trailing only Quinnen Williams. Rookie Dillon Thieneman also shines with a targeted passer rating of just 67.3 allowed. The run defense remains weak, with a wide gap between the team’s elite pass rush and its poor run stopping. One Bad Play Ruins The Grade Defensive tackle Grady Jarrett knows exactly what the issue is. He wants the yards per carry number under four, ideally under 3.5. The team allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to spike that average to 4.5 thanks to one specific run. No one reached the left-side B gap, but Bucky Irving escaped three tackles to gain 25 yards. Jarrett admits the fix is simple but hard. “We’ve got to eliminate those things,” Jarrett said. “These one-off plays are throwing off our average.” The Bears have the best third-down defense in the league, holding opponents to a 22.8% conversion rate. That stat puts them ahead of the 2019 Patriots record. But they also allow touchdowns 53.8% of the time in the red zone, which ranks 12th. The team has the talent to win, but the execution fails in the most critical spots. Can They Fix It Before Sunday? The bye week gave the coaching staff time to study the film. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has the résumé to fix these gaps. Before the Simmons trade, he demonstrated clever problem-solving abilities during his initial season and a half. The foundation is solid with creative pass-rush scheming and strong play from new additions. The offense is scoring, and the team sits at 7-2. But a championship run needs a defense that does not give up 25-yard runs late in the fourth quarter. The team must tighten up before the next game. Chicago hosts the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Soldier Field. This season, the Saints have not held the ball for more than 35 minutes in any single game.

item.title: Mets Pitch To Tarik Skubal As Clock Ticks Toward Lockout
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers starting pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) delivers in the fifth inning of a game against the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park in Detroit on Friday, Aug. 28, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tarik Skubal, the superstar pitcher, was met on Monday in Orange County, California by a high-powered group from the New York Mets. The New York Post reports this meeting was a direct pitch to win the two-time Cy Young winner for the upcoming season. Mets officials traveled west to make their case in person, signaling a serious intent to land the top free agent pitcher available. The team may have positioned itself as the first choice among six finalists in this winter’s biggest free agent derby. The incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two mystery teams were also granted meetings with Skubal. While the exact timing of the other sessions remains unknown, all are scheduled to happen sometime this week. The identities of the Mets officials who attended the Monday meeting were not revealed to the public. Early Signs Look Promising Word is that the session with Skubal went very well, though it remains hard to judge the full significance of that feeling right now. It is not known whether the Mets have made any official offers to Skubal yet. Time is short so there is a clear sense of urgency for all sides involved. Before the MLB lockout begins at 11:59 p.m. on December 1, Skubal is expected to sign. If a deal does not happen before that deadline, the league stops all player transactions until the lockout ends.

item.title: Arsenal face eight major contract decisions with four 'nearing deals'
item.description: Mikel Arteta's side is working to tie down its star players to new deals -Credit:David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images Arsenal have put in a huge amount of effort over the past 18 months to tie down their most important players to new deals. Since 2025, Gabriel, William Saliba, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman have all pledged their futures to the club. Mikel Arteta has been instrumental in those players' resolve to remain in North London, while the likes of James King, the club's head of football operations, and sporting director Andrea Berta have also played a pivotal role in the process. And this impressive track record shows no signs of letting up. Now, according to football.london , Declan Rice, Jurriën Timber and David Raya have all reportedly agreed to extend their stays at the club. Final details are still being ironed out, with announcements to follow in due course. Chris Richards sends message to Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT successor ahead of Man United move Ashley Young delivers brutal verdict on Man United squad ahead of Mauricio Pochettino's arrival Martin Odegaard is among those in the spotlight amid the Arsenal contract push -Credit:Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images Piero Hincapié is, surprisingly, another who, having joined on a permanent basis only in the summer of 2026, appears set for a revision of his deal as well. Arsenal have been known to renegotiate contract terms during the course of an existing deal to better reflect a player's contribution, as was previously the case with Raya and Leandro Trossard. There remain other players whose contracts have come under the club's scrutiny, without formal negotiations yet getting underway. Two such players are Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz. football.london dismissed reports from the summer that the club captain had agreed personal terms with Turkish club Galatasaray. Sources close to the player reiterated that he remains content at Arsenal, though no formal contract negotiations had yet commenced on his deal, which runs until 2028. While informal discussions are understood to have occurred, the player confirmed, "I'm happy and hope I can stay there [at Arsenal] for a long time to come, but we haven't started on that yet." item.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money
item.description: Luke Littler became world number one for the first time when he won the Grand Slam of Darts in 2025 [Press Association] The 2026 Grand Slam of Darts is under way and another of the Professional Darts Corporation's (PDC) major titles is set to be won in Wolverhampton. This edition is bigger than ever, with 48 players taking part, and unlike most of darts' major tournaments, the players are split into groups in the initial phase, rather than a straight knockout format. Each player will face two opponents in their group, with only the group winner progressing into the last 16. The rest of the competition is a straight knockout format. Luke Littler is the defending champion following a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries in the 2025 final to become world number one for the first time. Littler faces a tough start, with Beau Greaves his opponent on the opening evening, and Neils Zonneveld, who beat Littler in their only previous meeting, completing the group. When is the Grand Slam of Darts? The tournament lasts for nine days from Saturday, 14 November to Sunday, 22 November. Group stage (14-17 November) - 48 matches Second round (18-19 November) - eight matches Quarter-finals (20-21 November) Semi-finals (22 November) Final (22 November) What is the format? In the group stage, the format is best of nine legs, or first to five legs. In the initial phase, two points are awarded for a win, with the group winner progressing to the last 16. In case of players being level on points at the end of the group phase, the following tie-breakers apply: Total Leg Difference Total Legs Won Total Legs Won Against Throw Highest Total Tournament Average (to two decimal places) Highest Winning Match Average (to two decimal places) A play-off - nine-dart leg Second-round matches are a best-of-19 format, or first to 10 legs. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final are best of 31 legs, or first to 16 legs. Who is playing and how did they qualify? With the tournament expanded, a new set of qualification rules have been put in place. Up to 24 players could qualify from reaching a major PDC televised final in the past 12 months, but only nine ended up qualifying via that route, partly because of the dominance Littler has shown. Ten players reached Wolverhampton from the PDC youth, development and challenge tours, the Women's Matchplay and Women's Series and championships from across the globe. Six more secured places through the European Tour, while 13 qualified with a Players Championship win. The final 10 spots, which include ninth seed Stephen Bunting, were claimed in a PDC tour card holder qualifying event. From there, the top-16 ranked players in the PDC's order of merit were seeded and filled pot one. The next 16 went into pot two and the final 16 made up pot three. One player from each pot was then allocated to a group. Grand Slam of Darts groups, order of play & results Afternoon sessions start at 13:00 GMT, with evening sessions at 19:00 (19:30 on 15). Numbers in bra

item.title: Alexander Zverev wins rematch with Ben Shelton to reach ATP Finals last four
item.description: World No 1 Alexander Zverev reached the last four of the ATP Finals in Turin with a straight sets win over Ben Shelton . Zverev prevailed 6-2 7-6 (4) in a rematch of the US Open final earlier this year, which the German won in four sets to claim his second grand slam title. American Shelton had his serve broken in the first game of the opening set as Zverev stormed into a lead. A tighter contest followed in the second set as both players held their serve for the match to reach a tie-break, where Zverev was able to see out a second victory of the week. It means the French Open and US Open champion is through to the semi-finals ahead of his final match in the John McEnroe Group against Arthur Fils. Earlier on Tuesday, Fils claimed a maiden ATP Finals victory after coming from behind to beat Rafael Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2. Both players held their serve during the first set and following a lengthy deuce, Jodar clinched the ninth game before breaking in the next to take advantage. Fils took control in the second set, breaking Jodar’s serve twice and the Spanish player was forced to take two medical timeouts. The contest boiled down to a deciding set, where Fils eased to victory to become the first Frenchman since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011 to win an ATP Finals match. Fils lost his opening match of the tournament to Shelton on Sunday and was pleased with his response against Jodar. “I played great match against Ben, actually, I was just unlucky,” Fils said, in quotes reported on the ATP website. “Here, the first set was a bit ‘so so’ with a little bit of frustration. But I’m very happy with how I handled the second and the third, and a little bit of relief now.”

item.title: Lando Norris Says Wet Las Vegas Race Would Be Scary
item.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Lando Norris thinks the upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix could turn into a nightmare if it rains. The McLaren driver told Motorsport.com that the current tires simply do not work when the temperature drops too low. He called a wet practice session “scary” because the cars might lose grip on the cold track. The Cold Strip Problem The issue comes down to physics and the track layout. The Las Vegas circuit has long straights and very few high-speed corners. These corners usually help push heat into the rubber. Without them, the tires stay cold. Norris explained that the intermediate tires are useless in this cold weather. He said, “When the tyres get cold, it’s pretty nasty.” The cars feel horrible on the grid laps if the rubber cannot warm up. Drivers need a much better tire to handle the cold desert night. Drivers Agree on the Fix Max Verstappen, who finished second in Brazil, agrees with Norris. He told reporters that the working range for these tires is just too small. When they get hot, they are fine. When they get cold, they feel like a rock. Verstappen said, “I think it’s mainly that the working range is a bit too small.” He believes the team needs to find a way to make the tires work better in mixed conditions. Carlos Sainz also weighed in. The Williams driver feels the entire range of wet tires needs improvement. He thinks the level of the wet and intermediate tires is not good enough for the job. What Happens Next The race is set for Saturday, November 21, at 11 pm ET. The weather forecast shows a chance of rain over 50 percent for the first practice on Thursday evening. If it rains, drivers will have to deal with these cold, slippery tires. Norris noted that the scary times happen when you go to Vegas and cannot get any tire temperature. The race consists of 50 laps on the 3.853‑mile street circuit. A full wet race could be horrible without a better tire solution.

item.title: Cam Newton Says Dallas Must Swap For Brian Flores
item.description: Cam Newton on the sidelines during the Magic City Classic at Legion Field in Birmingham, Ala., on Saturday, October 31, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Cam Newton has a clear answer for the Dallas Cowboys’ defensive mess. The former quarterback says the team should have traded for Brian Flores instead of hiring Christian Parker. Newton believes the Vikings coach is the missing piece Dallas needs to stop giving up points. The numbers back up Newton’s frustration. The Vikings are the best defensive unit in the league right now. They are letting in only 14 points per game. That is two fewer points than the Seattle Seahawks allow. Brian Flores has turned Minnesota into a stopper while Dallas struggles to find a way to win. Newton said the trade was possible and necessary. The Case for a Trade Newton thinks Dallas missed a huge chance to fix their roster. He stated, “They should have been able to trade not just players, but coaches. They should have traded Brian Flores for Christian Parker.” The idea was to get a proven winner instead of a young coach with less experience. Parker won a Super Bowl in Philadelphia as a defensive backs coach. But he has not been able to stop the bleeding in Dallas. Jerry Jones, having dismissed Matt Eberflus, sought a total overhaul of the unit. Jones started that process by bringing in Parker. Ten games into the season now, numerous analysts feel this experiment has failed significantly. The defense has been terrible for years. They were 31st in points allowed in 2024. They fell to 32nd in 2025. They are 30th in points allowed in 2026. The trend is not getting better. Rex Ryan Takes Aim Rex Ryan is not holding back either. The ESPN analyst has repeatedly jabbed at Jerry Jones for not hiring him. Ryan called the current group the worst coached defense he has ever seen. He spoke on ESPN New York on Monday. Ryan said, “It really is. And I’ve seen some horrible defenses, this one’s awful, and it starts with coaching.” He believes the players are making too many mental mistakes. Ryan claims he could fix the unit in just one week. He told the network, “I could go there today and say, ‘Alright, we can have an average ass defense.” He promised he would take the current group and turn it around quickly. The Cowboys have given up a lot of yardage and points. Newton noted, “There’s no way that you give up that amount of yardage and expect to win.” The team faces the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium.

item.title: Simmons Calls Patriots A.J. Brown Deal Worst In Boston History
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The New England Patriots acquired A.J. Brown in a move that now looks like a disaster. Bill Simmons called the deal “one of the worst trades in Boston sports history” on his podcast. This harsh take comes after Brown played just four games and caught only 11 passes for 128 yards. The 29-year-old receiver missed time with a high ankle sprain, a knee issue, and now a hamstring injury. In Munich, that fresh injury forced him out of Sunday’s 35-10 defeat against the Detroit Lions. While addressing the trade and Brown’s most recent injury, Simmons offered no restraint. He compared the current situation to the failed N’Keal Harry pick in 2019. Brown has yet to score a touchdown in his first season with the team. Acquiring him cost the Patriots a 2028 first-round selection plus a 2027 fifth-round pick. That price tag feels much higher now that the player is hurt again. Simmons noted that the team kept Brown on the field even when the game was out of hand. Regarding a player not at 100% on a dreadful Munich field, he queried what could possibly go wrong. Former Players Are Unhappy Too Rob Gronkowski is not happy with how the trade has played out so far. The former Patriots tight end admitted on his show that the move has been a letdown. “It’s been a disappointment, you know, the disappointing trade so far,” Gronkowski said. He stressed that Brown has not lived up to the hype after the team sent a first-rounder for him. Shannon Sharpe also criticized Brown for leaving the Philadelphia Eagles. Sharpe said on his podcast that Brown “brought this on himself” by complaining about his role in Philly. He pointed out that Brown was unhappy even when the Eagles were winning football games. The Cost of a Broken Deal The numbers show a clear struggle for the wide receiver. Through Week 10, Brown recorded 11 receptions, 128 yards, and zero touchdowns. He missed six of the first nine games due to various injuries. Former Patriots receiver Chad Johnson noted that Brown’s confidence might be shot. “I think right now AJ’s confidence might be shot just a little bit, just because of the drops,” Johnson said, according to a report . The team now sits at 5-5 and enters its bye week. Brown will have two weeks to heal before facing the Los Angeles Chargers on November 29.

item.title: Chiefs Rookies Johnson And Allen Shine In Atlanta Win
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Rookie running back Emmett Johnson scored two touchdowns and caught six passes for 70 yards in Sunday’s blowout win over the Atlanta Falcons. The Kansas City Chiefs rolled to a 35-13 victory at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Nov. 15, with Johnson filling in for the injured Kenneth Walker III. This performance marks a major shift for a squad that struggled last season and needed a roster reset to compete again. Allen Finds End Zone Wide receiver Cyrus Allen also broke through on Sunday by scoring his first career touchdown against a top-tier cornerback. Allen beat Atlanta’s A.J. Terrell on a double move to seal the deal in the second half. The Associated Press noted that Allen helped injured‑reserve wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, giving the offense a needed boost. Chiefs coach Andy Reid praised the young group after the game, noting their rapid improvement. “We’re one of the youngest teams in the league and they’re getting better every week,” Reid said. He added that the coaching staff must be patient with these players as they grow into their roles. “It’s good that the coaches keep coaching them. Got to have a little patience with them, but they’re doing a heck of a job,” Reid said. The team had 10 rookies active for the game, a number that highlights the depth the franchise is building for the long haul. Depth Tested by Injuries The young players stepped up because the Chiefs face a wave of injuries at key positions. Left tackle Kahlil Benson played well in place of Josh Simmons, who is now on injured reserve. R Mason Thomas, the defensive end, also made contributions, although this specific game marked the first time he recorded zero pressure throughout his KC tenure. Sports Illustrated ranked Johnson and Allen at the top of their rookie and sophomore power rankings, calling them the best of the bunch. The team faces the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22, at Arrowhead Stadium for their next matchup.

item.title: Mike McCarthy Waits On Mason McCormick’s Brutal Ankle Diagnosis
item.description: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Head coach Mike McCarthy still lacks a final diagnosis for Mason McCormick after the offensive lineman suffered a gruesome ankle injury. The Steelers lost 38-18 to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday night, but the score now matters less than the health of their key guard. McCormick’s right ankle turned in the wrong direction late in the second quarter, forcing trainers to cart him off the field. This marks the first time in his career the 26-year-old veteran will miss games. He had started 39 straight contests before Sunday. Now, the entire roster waits for news from the training room. No Diagnosis Yet McCarthy told reporters on Monday that the team is still gathering information on the injury. He did not have a clear answer on when the guard might return. “Mike McCarthy says they’re still gathering information on G Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury last night,” Brooke Pryor reported for Yahoo Sports . The coach emphasized the need for patience while doctors work. The situation remains fluid as the medical staff reviews the scans. McCarthy noted that McCormick showed a great attitude while sitting in the room, but the timeline is still unknown. The team cannot move forward until they know the full extent of the damage. A Leader in the Room The loss of McCormick hits hard because he is viewed as a captain by his teammates. He has been a steady presence in the line, earning a 76.1 overall grade from Pro Football Focus this season. That score ranked 14th among 75 qualified guards. His run-blocking grade of 77.3 placed 10th at his position. Teammates are visibly upset by the sight of his injury. “Steelers offensive linemen are crushed after seeing what happened to Mason McCormick. Troy Fautanu said he was sick to his stomach after witnessing the injury,” Ray Fittipaldo posted on X. McCarthy confirmed the leadership role McCormick holds. The void he leaves is significant for the unit. The Backup Plan Spencer Anderson is the only backup guard currently available on the roster. Anderson took McCormick’s place at left guard after the injury occurred. The team is likely to be without the veteran for multiple weeks given the severity of the injury. McCarthy expressed hope for other players to return soon. The Steelers must now navigate the rest of the season without their most consistent starter. The next game for the team is scheduled for Sunday, Nov. 22, against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. The team will face a tough test on the road with a depleted offensive line.

item.title: CJ McCollum injury update deals Hawks’ bench a brutal setback
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images CJ McCollum injury update deals Hawks’ bench a brutal setback appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Hawks have had an up-and-down start to the 2026-27 NBA season, currently sitting at 8-6 following a recent road win over the Milwaukee Bucks . On Tuesday, the Hawks got a tough injury update regarding a key veteran member of the team. “ CJ McCollum sustained a left leg injury during Sunday’s game at Milwaukee. Following a medical evaluation and imaging, he has been diagnosed with a left calf strain. McCollum will be re-evaluated in approximately four weeks, and an update will be provided at that time,” reported the Hawks on X, formerly Twitter. That wasn’t the end of the bad news for Atlanta, as the Hawks also announced that 2025 first-round draft pick Asa Newell had undergone surgery on a plantar plate tear and would be out for at least four months. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCollum had suffered through a tough start to the season for Atlanta, at one point voluntarily benching himself for rookie Kingston Flemings and hoping to be a spark plug off the Hawks’ bench. While he hasn’t shot with his usual efficiency so far this year, McCollum is still one of the few Hawks players who can reliably create his own shot in the half-court, so soldiering forward without him for the foreseeable future will certainly be a challenge. Meanwhile, Newell has seen very limited playing time in his NBA career thus far, but this injury setback will obviously hurt his chances of taking a leap this season. item.title: Gamecocks Fans Got Their Wish And It Cost Them A Playoff Spot
item.description: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images South Carolina fans who begged coach Shane Beamer to sit Heisman hopeful LaNorris Sellers against Arkansas got exactly what they asked for. The result was a loss that ended the team’s College Football Playoff hopes. According to a report , the Gamecocks played the Razorbacks missing their leading quarterback, leading running back, and leading deep threat. This lineup was not a recipe for success, and the night game in the SEC proved anything can happen. The team’s dreams of a playoff spot died in Arkansas on a Saturday night. The injury to Sellers was the main reason for the change, but the decision carried heavy weight. Sellers suffered an ankle injury against Texas A&M that lingered into the Arkansas game. He warmed up before the contest, but that was likely just gamesmanship by the coaching staff. Backup quarterback Cutter Woods stepped in to lead the offense with 24 of 43 passes for 271 yards. Woods showed mobility and arm strength that had been overlooked in past outings. However, three interceptions, including a pick six when momentum shifted, hurt the team. Beamer explained the choice after the game, noting the physical limitations of the starter. The Cost of a Bench Decision Beamer stated his reasoning clearly regarding the decision to start Woods over Sellers. “We just felt like from a physical standpoint, just wasn’t to the point where we felt like (Sellers) gave us the best chance,” Beamer said. The coach added that “Cutter gave us the best chance.” These words came out after the Gamecocks lost to Arkansas. The loss was a direct result of playing a backup quarterback who struggled with turnovers. Fans who wanted Sellers to sit now face a team that cannot reach the postseason. The roster was already thin before the game. Running back Matt Fuller was lost for the season with a broken foot a couple of games ago. Nyck Harbor, a wide receiver, was also absent from the game due to injury. The team had to play without its best weapons at every offensive skill position. This lack of depth made the backup quarterback’s job nearly impossible against a tough SEC defense. The three interceptions included a pick six. Heisman Dreams Still Alive? Even with the loss, Sellers remains in the race for the Heisman Trophy. Should his performance match the four prior wins, victory remains possible. The Gamecocks must beat No. 1 Georgia on Saturday night to keep their hopes alive. A strong performance against Clemson would also be required to make Sellers a finalist. The path is narrow, but the award is still possible if the team wins its remaining games. The loss in Arkansas did not remove him from the conversation entirely. The team had beaten nationally ranked Florida and Tennessee in their four-game streak. Fans thought the Gamecocks would make easy work of a struggling Arkansas team. Instead, the injury to Sellers and the loss of other key players led to a defeat. The fans who wanted Sellers to sit now see the consequences of tha

item.title: How does Euro 2028 qualifying work? Confirmed pots, format, and rules for co-hosts
item.description: Co-hosted on home soil by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, the road to Euro 2028 is fast approaching as the draw for qualifying takes place in Belfast in early December. But the four co-hosts will enter qualifying for the tournament as normal, even though there is a ‘safety net’ that can be used by two of the teams should they fail to qualify automatically. The United Kingdom hosted some games during the Covid-delayed Euro 2020 tournament in 2021, although many matches were played with limited capacities due to Covid restrictions. Wembley hosted the final and will do so again in 2028, with Cardiff, Glasgow, Dublin, Birmingham, Liverpool, Manchester, Newcastle also staging games during the 24-team tournament. Here’s everything you need to know ahead of the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place in Northern Ireland on Sunday 6 December. Confirmed Euro 2028 qualifying pots Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, England (co-host), France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Northern Ireland , Republic of Ireland (co-host), Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, Wales (co-host) Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland (co-host) Slovakia, Ukraine Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino Pot 5: Andorra, Azerbaijan, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Malta How does Euro 2028 qualifying work? The 54 competing Uefa teams will be drawn into 12 groups; Groups A-F are groups of four, while Groups G-L are groups of five Teams competing in the Nations League quarter-finals or Nations League promotion/relegation play-offs will be treated differently in the draw Nations League quarter-final winners will be placed into groups of four, while groups of five can only feature one Nations League quarter-final loser, or a play-off team The 12 group winners will qualify automatically, followed by the eight best-ranked runners-up based on qualifying results As many as four additional places could be up for grabs in the qualifying play-offs, but that could go down to two if two of the co-hosts fail to qualify automatically The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals and Nations League play-offs will take place on Friday and will have an impact on the Euro 2028 qualifying draw What teams are still involved in the Nations League? item.content:encoded: Co-hosted on home soil by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland, the road to Euro 2028 is fast approaching as the draw for qualifying takes place in Belfast in early December. But the four co-hosts will enter qualifying for the tournament as normal, even though there is a ‘safety net’ that can be used by two of the teams should they fail to qualify automatically. The United Kingdom hosted some games during the Covid-delayed Euro 2020 tournament in 2021, although many matches were played with limited capacities due to Covid restrictions. Wembley hosted the final and will do so again in 2028, with Cardiff, Glasgow, Dublin, Birmingham, Liverpool, Manchester, Newcastle also staging games during the 24-team tournament. Here’s everything you need to know ahead of the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place in Northern Ireland on Sunday 6 December. Confirmed Euro 2028 qualifying pots Pot 1: Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, England (co-host), France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain Pot 2: Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Hungary, Northern Ireland , Republic of Ireland (co-host), Serbia, Slovenia, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, Wales (co-host) Pot 3: Albania, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Scotland (co-host) Slovakia, Ukraine Pot 4: Armenia, Belarus, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia, Faroe Islands, Finland, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Moldova, San Marino Pot 5: Andorra, Azerbaijan, Gibraltar, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Malta How does Euro 2028 qualifying work? The 54 competing Uefa teams will be drawn into 12 groups; Groups A-F are groups of four, while Groups G-L are groups of five Teams competing in the Nations League quarter-finals or Nations League promotion/relegation play-offs will be treated differently in the draw Nations League quarter-final winners will be placed into groups of four, while groups of five can only feature one Nations League quarter-final loser, or a play-off team The 12 group winners will qualify automatically, followed by the eight best-ranked runners-up based on qualifying results As many as four additional places could be up for grabs in the qualifying play-offs, but that could go down to two if two of the co-hosts fail to qualify automatically The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals and Nations League play-offs will take place on Friday and will have an impact on the Euro 2028 qualifying draw What teams are still involved in the Nations League? Nations League quarter-finals Group winners: France, Germany, England, Portugal Group runners-up: Belgium, Netherlands, Spain, Norway Nations League play-offs: League A/B League A third/fourth place: Croatia, Denmark, Serbia, Wales League B runners-up: Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republic of Ireland, Hungary Nations League play-offs: League B/C League B fourth place: North Macedonia, Romania, Israel, Georgia League C runner-up: Belarus, Cyprus, Faroe Islands, Estonia England will not start their Euro 2028 campaign until September if they reach the Nations League Finals (Getty) What are the rules for the co-hosts? Unlike previous major tournaments held in multiple countries, England , Scotland , Wales and the Republic of Ireland do not qualify automatically just because they are co-hosts. Although this is a tournament for the UK and Ireland, Northern Ireland are not considered co-hosts, as they are not staging any games. But while England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland all enter qualifying as usual, there are two reserved places to be used by co-hosts if they fail to qualify automatically , either by winning their group or finishing as one of the eight-best runners-up. The four co-hosts , as well as Northern Ireland for that matter, will all be kept apart in the qualifying draw to boost their qualification chances, so if they all go on to their win their groups then happy days – the safety net is not required. But if disaster strikes and three or more of the co-hosts fail to qualify on merit, then there are just the two reserved places to fall back on: they will go to the two teams who have the best record in qualifying and the others will have to watch on. Scotland fell into Pot 3 of the Euro 2028 draw by finishing third in League B of the Nations League (PA) When is the draw and when does qualifying take place? The Euro 2028 qualifying draw takes place in Belfast on Sunday 6 December. Qualifying then begins in March 2027, but only for the teams not involved in the Nations League quarter-finals or Nations League play-offs who were drawn into Groups G-L. Within those groups of five, the four other teams will play against each other across March and June 2027, with everyone else then beginning their qualifying campaign from September 2027. Matchday 1: 26–27 March 2027 (groups of five only) Matchday 2: 29–30 March 2027 (groups of five only) Matchday 3: 11–12 June 2027 (groups of five only) Matchday 4: 14–15 June 2027 (groups of five only) Matchday 5: 23–25 September 2027 Matchday 6: 26–28 September 2027 Matchday 7: 30 September – 2 October 2027 Matchday 8: 3–5 October 2027 Matchday 9: 11–13 November 2027 Matchday 10: 14–16 November 2027

item.title: Penn State’s LS In the Running for the Patrick Mannelly Award
item.description: STATE COLLEGE, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 19: Ryan Barker #94 of the Penn State Nittany Lions reacts after making a field goal during the second quarter against the Buffalo Bulls at Beaver Stadium on September 19, 2026 in State College, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) Getty Penn State football’s Blaise Sokach-Minnick was announced as a semifinalist for the Patrick Mannelly Award, given to the nation’s top long snapper, on Monday night. Blaise becomes the third straight Nittany Lion to be named a semifinalist for this award. Blaise → Mannelly Award Semifinalist 🎯 @blaisesm15 pic.twitter.com/pOC9pFVt2Z — Penn State Football (@PennStateFball) November 17, 2026 The Patrick Mannelly Award, named after former Duke LS Patrick Mannelly, benefits Bernie’s Book Bank , a nonprofit organization that sources, processes, and distributes free books to children. The redshirt senior is one of 10 semifinalists for the award and is gunning to become a top-three finalist, with the finalists announced on November 30. During preseason, Blaise was on the Mannelly Award Watch List . He follows former Penn State finalists Chris Stoll, who won the award in 2022, and Tyler Duzansky. Blaise has appeared in 16 career games, including 10 as the team’s primary snapper this season, and recorded one career solo tackle vs. Buffalo on September 19. He aided Penn State kicker Ryan Barker in converting 12 field goals and went a perfect 35/35 on extra points, and helped punter Nathan Tiyce average 41.2 yards per punt, placing 15 punts inside the 20-yard line with three boots of 50+ yards. Blaise also served as a team captain against Marshall and Michigan this season. The Patrick Mannelly Award winner will be announced on December 12 at the Mannelly Award ceremony in Lake Bluff, Illinois. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Penn State’s LS In the Running for the Patrick Mannelly Award appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Molly Miller making Arizona State ‘school of choice’ for top basketball recruits
item.description: By now, if you’re a fan of women’s college basketball , you know exactly who Molly Miller is. The Arizona State head coach is one of the hottest names in the coaching world and has the ability to go viral each and every week. Miller has had success as a coach at every one of her stops, but her popularity has reached new heights now that she’s at Arizona State. Whether it be her press conferences and knack for motivational quotes or her stellar style she brings to the sideline every game , Miller has everyone’s attention. And now, top recruits are included in that “everyone.” This week, No. 1 overall recruit Kaleena Smith announced her top three schools : USC, UCLA, and Arizona State. UConn made an in-home visit to California, but Geno Auriemma’s powerhouse squad is no longer in the mix, while Miller’s Sun Devils are. MORE: Arizona State basketball coach Molly Miller turns heads in wrap-around skirt vs Penn State Molly Miller Making Waves On & Off Court Oct 20, 2026; Kansas City, MO, USA; Arizona State coach Molly Miller interviews during the Big 12 Media Days event at T-Mobile Center. Mandatory Credit: William Purnell-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Miller was asked for her thoughts on the consensus No. 1 overall program placing Arizona State on her shortlist, and she immediately thought of the big picture. Hopefully, this won’t be a one-time thing, because Miller is building ASU into a “school of choice” for top recruits. “What a cool feeling to feel like we’ve become a school of choice , whether that’s recruiting freshmen, whether that’s recruiting in the portal, the brand’s exciting for the fans. It’s exciting for the players to play. There’s real momentum and buzz,” Miller told Echo From The Buttes’ Aya Abdeen. MORE: ASU cheerleaders greet Molly Miller, new Sun Devils women’s basketball coach “And when you can be a part of that momentum and create something special and kind of build it as it rises, I think these recruits are excited about that. We’re looking for recruits that kind of want to mark their own territory and make their own stamp in this journey.” Arizona State women’s basketball head coach Molly Miller yells out to her team as they play the Jackson State Tigers at Desert Financial Arena in Tempe on Nov. 2, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Smith, despite standing just 5-foot-6, would be a major get for the Sun Devils. The standout guard from Ontario Christian School averaged 31.5 points, 6.9 assists, 4.5 steals, and 3.7 rebounds per game. She was named the MaxPreps National Player of the Year. MORE: Arizona State women’s basketball coach Molly Miller rewarded after breakout season Smith also earned a gold medal as part of the 2026 FIBA U18 Women’s AmeriCup team, averaging 19.8 points and 6.4 assists per game. Wherever she lands, there is no denying the dynamic guard is going to be a bona fide star, and if Miller could land the top recruit in the country, it would be a pro

item.title: Patriots eye veteran QB despite Tommy DeVito remaining the expected starter
item.description: Patriots eye veteran QB despite Tommy DeVito remaining the expected starter originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots have a quarterback situation, or maybe we can even call it a situationship because it's complicated. Drake Maye went down with a nasty injury during the team's game overseas against the Detroit Lions , and the direct backup to him is New Jersey guy Tommy DeVito. But DeVito isn't exactly a veteran quarterback. Other than his stint with the New York Giants , he hasn't been in a real NFL situation for a long time. There are veterans out there, and Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is reportedly looking into that. New England Patriots exploring quarterback market after Drake Maye injury League insider Jordan Schultz reports that the team is currently looking for another quarterback after having to turn to DeVito. However, he adds that DeVito is expected to be the starter unless the Patriots are able to pull a bunny out of their hat. "The #Patriots are expected to explore the QB market during the bye week, from free agents such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who has previously played for OC Josh McDaniels, to potentially adding a QB off another team's practice squad," Schultz posted to X on Monday, Nov. 16 . "Tommy DeVito is currently expected to become the starter." The Patriots could also look to poach someone from a practice squad. So even though the trade deadline is over, they have options. New England's record is 5-5, and they're No. 2 in the AFC East. They're in that position where they're good enough to possibly make the playoffs, but it's probably not worth giving an arm and a leg to get a Maye fill-in and risk anything for the future of the franchise. More NFL news: Tommy DeVito has mixed New England Patriots performance filling in for Drake Maye Mike Vrabel makes gutting comments in Munich Steelers and Aaron Rodgers’ playoff chances officially revealed John Harbaugh and Giants looking ‘shakier’ as New York makes a playoff push

item.title: Cubs’ Seiya Suzuki Makes $23.15 Million Contract Decision
item.description: Blue Jays predicted to sign Seiya Suzuki. Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 04: Seiya Suzuki #27 of the Chicago Cubs flies out during the seventh inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on September 04, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Getty Seiya Suzuki Cubs Getty The Chicago Cubs and Seiya Suzuki turned out to be a great pairing. It’s just not clear whether they’ll spend any more time together. Nov. 17 marked a key day in the relationship between the Cubs and Suzuki, because it’s qualifying offer decision day. Suzuki had previously been extended the qualifying offer by the Cubs. If accepted, it would pay him $23.15 million to play for Chicago in the 2027 MLB season. If declined by Suzuki, the Cubs get compensation if he signs anywhere else in free agency. On Tuesday, Suzuki made his initial choice. Seiya Suzuki Contract Decision Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA – SEPTEMBER 04: Seiya Suzuki #27 of the Chicago Cubs flies out during the seventh inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on September 04, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Suzuki has chosen to decline the qualifying offer, according to MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand . Seiya Suzuki is declining the qualifying offer from the Cubs, per source. — Mark Feinsand (@Feinsand) November 17, 2026 It wasn’t a particular surprise. Suzuki believes he can get a multi-year deal on the open market, potentially for close to that $20 million per year kind of range. Suzuki could’ve decided to return to the Cubs for that $23.15 million figure, but there’s no guarantee that next offseason he would be as sought-after as he will be this offseason. It’s best for Suzuki to try and cash in while he can, and that appears to be what he’s doing. He’s not the only player to decline the qualifying offer on Tuesday afternoon in the NL Central. Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe did the same thing. As expected, Brandon Lowe will decline the $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Pirates, sources confirm to https://t.co/RA5WrbJUwA . item.content:encoded: Blue Jays predicted to sign Seiya Suzuki. Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 04: Seiya Suzuki #27 of the Chicago Cubs flies out during the seventh inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on September 04, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Getty Seiya Suzuki Cubs Getty The Chicago Cubs and Seiya Suzuki turned out to be a great pairing. It’s just not clear whether they’ll spend any more time together. Nov. 17 marked a key day in the relationship between the Cubs and Suzuki, because it’s qualifying offer decision day. Suzuki had previously been extended the qualifying offer by the Cubs. If accepted, it would pay him $23.15 million to play for Chicago in the 2027 MLB season. If declined by Suzuki, the Cubs get compensation if he signs anywhere else in free agency. On Tuesday, Suzuki made his initial choice. Seiya Suzuki Contract Decision Getty MIAMI, FLORIDA – SEPTEMBER 04: Seiya Suzuki #27 of the Chicago Cubs flies out during the seventh inning against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on September 04, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Suzuki has chosen to decline the qualifying offer, according to MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand . Seiya Suzuki is declining the qualifying offer from the Cubs, per source. — Mark Feinsand (@Feinsand) November 17, 2026 It wasn’t a particular surprise. Suzuki believes he can get a multi-year deal on the open market, potentially for close to that $20 million per year kind of range. Suzuki could’ve decided to return to the Cubs for that $23.15 million figure, but there’s no guarantee that next offseason he would be as sought-after as he will be this offseason. It’s best for Suzuki to try and cash in while he can, and that appears to be what he’s doing. He’s not the only player to decline the qualifying offer on Tuesday afternoon in the NL Central. Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe did the same thing. As expected, Brandon Lowe will decline the $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Pirates, sources confirm to https://t.co/RA5WrbJUwA . If Lowe were to sign elsewhere for $50 million or more, Pittsburgh would now receive a Draft pick between the first round and Competitive… https://t.co/e0ClyIDwS2 — Aiden Stepansky (@AidenStepansky) November 17, 2026 Seiya Suzuki Landing Spot Getty SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 30: Seiya Suzuki #27 of the Chicago Cubs looks on before game two of the National League Wild Card Series against the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on September 30, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) One team has been rumored more than any other as the club that can land Suzuki in free agency: the Toronto Blue Jays. Toronto had great success with Japanese star Kazuma Okamoto in 2026 and could use the right-handed bat and outfield presence that Suzuki brings. The Blue Jays have also shown themselves willing to pay up in recent years. They haven’t landed all the players they’ve pursued — including losing out to the Dodgers on both Shohei Ohtani and Kyle Tucker — but that won’t stop Toronto from really going after the guys they want. Suzuki will have other suitors, although the Dodgers aren’t likely among that group. If Suzuki does indeed end up somewhere other than Chicago this offseason, don’t be surprised if it’s Toronto.
