item.title: Giants’ Zvada Struggles Spark Debate Over Ben Sauls Options
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada is drawing sharp criticism from a loud group of New York Giants fans who want him off the roster. The pressure comes after a rough stretch where the young kicker missed six of his last 14 field-goal attempts. While the start of the season looked perfect with nine straight makes, the last four games have shown clear cracks in his game. Per Big Blue View , a vocal part of the fan base believes the team should have already booted Zvada to the curb. Head coach John Harbaugh pushed back against the idea of making a quick change during the week. “You can’t, as soon as a guy doesn’t make a play, start firing people left and right,” he said. He noted that finding a new player who is definitely better is much harder than just saying someone has to go. The Case for Keeping Zvada Blowing the whistle on Zvada right now might not fix the real problem. Per Big Blue View, the main issue is a much-discussed problem from the right hash mark that has cost the team points. Even with the misses, Zvada has proven he can hit the big shots that other kickers might dread. Why Ben Sauls Is Not the Answer Many fans point to left-footed Ben Sauls as the savior who could fix the kicking woes. Sauls was an elixir for the Giants at the end of the 2025 season, making all 15 of his kicks over a three-game span. His record included eight field goals and seven extra points, with a longest kick of 45 yards. However, the Giants cannot just call him up if he is not on the team. Big Blue View reports that Ben Sauls is not on a 53-man roster or practice squad at this time. There is also a question of whether Sauls can handle the long kicks Zvada attempts. While Sauls was great in the spring and summer, he had his own technique issues before the season started. During summer practice, he was not nearly as consistent as Zvada, having been terrible in the spring by consistently pushing kicks to the left. When the two kickers competed for the spot, deciding which of them should win the job was easily done. The Harbaugh Reality Check John Harbaugh knows that swapping players is easy in theory but hard in practice. The Giants do not have a ready-made replacement sitting on the bench who can hit 50-yarders with confidence. The Giants will face the Jacksonville Jaguars next on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 4:25 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

item.title: Devon Dampier wins multiple national weekly awards
item.description: Utah quarterback Devon Dampier scores a touchdown in front of Arizona safety Gavin Hunter (23) in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press The awards are pouring in this week for Utah quarterback Devon Dampier after he led the No. 2 Utes to a 40-39 victory over No. 23 Arizona on Saturday night. Dampier accounted for 304 yards and four touchdowns and threw a 70-yard touchdown to Creed Whittemore for the win, which improved the Utes’ record to 10-0. The senior quarterback was named the Big 12’s co-offensive player of the week for the second consecutive time, but also received two national awards. Dampier was named the Maxwell Award Player of the Week and the Davey O’Brien National Quarterback of the Week. The Maxwell Award is given to the best all-around player in college football at the end of the season, while the Davey O’Brien Award is given to the nation’s best quarterback. Dampier has thrown for 2,257 yards and 22 touchdowns and rushed for 582 yards and nine scores this season. He has been one of the best quarterbacks in all of college football this year and currently has the third-best odds to win the Heisman Trophy. Utah Utes quarterback Devon Dampier (4) dances in celebration after scoring a touchdown during a game against Kansas at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News

item.title: Ex-Steelers OL Says Pittsburgh Was 'Exposed,' 'Embarrassed' in Loss to Bengals
item.description: Ex-Steelers OL Says Pittsburgh Was 'Exposed,' 'Embarrassed' in Loss to Bengals originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Steelers never had a chance against the Bengals on Sunday night, suffering a 38-18 defeat in an AFC North battle. Pittsburgh (6-3) is only one game behind Cincinnati (7-2) in the standings, but former Steelers offensive lineman Willie Colon believes that Mike McCarthy's squad was "exposed" in the blowout loss. "The blueprint is out, how to beat the hell out of the Pittsburgh Steelers," Colon said during Monday's episode of the "Bart and Willie Show" with former NFL linebacker Bart Scott. Colon, who won a Super Bowl with the Steelers in 2009, told Scott that Cincinnati attacked all of Pittsburgh's biggest flaws. Joe Burrow and the Bengals' offense put the Steelers in an early hole, and Pittsburgh was unable to match that level of firepower. "What you showed was, from the defense's standpoint, that if you win the line of scrimmage, take away their run game, neutralize their tight ends and force their wideouts to beat you, it's over," Colon said. "And that's what happened. ... This team isn't built to go toe-to-toe with anybody. This team is built to grind it out through four quarters, lean on their defense." Colon noted that Pittsburgh's pass rushers couldn't consistently put pressure on Burrow, who threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns. The Bengals finished with 484 yards of total offense (7.4 yards per play), while the Steelers produced just 222 total yards (3.8 yards per play). "We got exposed," Colon said. "We got embarrassed on primetime television." More Steelers Latest Steelers news How 'Renegade' became Steelers' pump-up song Complete history of Steelers championships

item.title: BIG10 Secures 7 Berths in NCAA Men’s Soccer Tournament
item.description: The Washington Huskies celebrate after winning the 2025 NCAA Men's Soccer Championship in Cary, N.C. Getty The Big Ten Conference has placed seven teams in the NCAA Division I Men’s Soccer Championship led by defending national champion Washington and No. 1 seed Indiana. All first-round matches in the 48-team bracket will be held at campus sites Thursday. Three weeks of competition will conclude with the 68th NCAA Men’s College Cup on Dec. 11 and 14 in Cary, N.C. Joining the Huskies and Hoosiers in this year’s tournament field are Maryland, Rutgers, Michigan State, Wisconsin and UCLA. The Big Ten’s seven tourney teams are the most in conference history, topping the six which qualified two years ago. Defending champion Washington makes its 31st tournament appearance. The No. 5-seeded Huskies (10-4-5) play host to Cleveland State (9-6-4) Thursday at 10 p.m. (ET). Their quadrant is loaded with talent that includes top-seeded Indiana and No. 2 seed Maryland. Indiana (15-1-4) won both the Big Ten regular-season and tournament titles. The Hoosiers claim the No. 3 overall seed among the 48 teams, behind only Georgetown and SMU. Their lone loss this season came Oct. 16 at Rutgers, 1-0. Washington, Indiana Could Be Headed for Rematch IU is making its 51st NCAA Tournament appearance and drew a first-round bye. It’ll open play at home Sunday at 12 p.m. (ET) against the winner of Thursday’s Missouri State-Saint Louis match. If Washington and Indiana were to reach the third round, they would meet Nov. 28/29 in a rematch of last weekend’s Big Ten Tournament championship won by the Hoosiers, 3-2, in a penalty kick shootout. This is the 43rd tournament appearance for Maryland (12-5-1) and, like Indiana, the Terrapins drew a first-round bye. They’ll open Sunday at 1 p.m. (ET) by hosting the winner of the North Carolina State-College of Charleston match. Rutgers earned a No. 3 seed and will begin tournament play Sunday at 6 p.m. (ET) against either Cornell or Fairleigh Dickinson. The Scarlet Knights (9-6-3) are making their 19th tournament appearance in a quadrant that also includes No. 4 seed UCLA. Michigan State Gets Home Field for Opening Match The Bruins (9-4-5) are among the six Big Ten teams with first-round byes and will debut in the tournament Sunday at 7 p.m. (ET) at home against either Creighton or Omaha. They could potentially meet Rutgers in the quarterfinals Dec. 4/5. Michigan State (10-5-3), seeded No. 4 in its quadrant, returns to the tournament for the first time since 2018 and also enjoys a first-round bye. The Spartans kick off their title bid at home Sunday at 2 p.m. (ET) opposite either Marshall or Bowling Green. Wisconsin (10-3-4), also seeded No. 4 in its quadrant, is in the tournament for the first time since 2017 and will kick off Sunday at 3 p.m. (ET) in Madison against the winner of Thursday’s first-round match between Charlotte and Lehigh. All second-round matches will take place Sunday with the third round scheduled for Saturday and Sun

item.title: Mike Gesicki & Dalton Kincaid Headline NFL Week 11 Fantasy Football Tight End Starts
item.description: Nov 15, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki (88) and running back Chase Brown (30) celebrate a touchdown during the second quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 11 cuts through the usual positional wasteland with a slate full of target monsters, mismatch nightmares, and defenses that flat-out refuse to cover the middle of the field. Whether you're riding with a blue-chip stud or rolling the dice on a streaming sleeper, lock these tight ends into your lineup and actually enjoy watching your production from the tight end position blossom. Tier 1: Must Start Tight Ends Trey McBride: The Weekly Matchup Nightmare Week 11 Matchup: Arizona Cardinals @ Kansas City Chiefs (Sunday, 12:00 PM CST) Nov 15, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride (85) looks on before the game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McBride continues to operate as the engine of the Arizona passing attack, cementing his status as an automatic, set-it-and-forget-it starter regardless of the opponent. Heading into a road clash at Arrowhead Stadium, McBride's elite target share, high route participation, and physicality after the catch insulate him from negative game scripts. If the Chiefs jump out to an early lead, expect Arizona to lean heavily on McBride, especially with a rookie quarterback under center . Last week against the Rams, he had his worst statistical game of the season with 5 receptions for 37 yards. It ended a streak of 11 consecutive games with at least seven catches, and also was the first time all season he was held below 10 fantasy points. Brock Bowers: Elite Production Regardless of Matchup Week 11 Matchup: Las Vegas Raiders @ Denver Broncos (Sunday, 3:25 PM CST) November 8, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (89) during the fourth quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bowers has proven completely matchup-proof, consistently commanding volume and manufacturing chunk plays even when opposing defenses bracket him. While a divisional trip to Mile High against Denver's disciplined defense poses a stiff test. Bowers versatility (lining up inline, in the slot, and out wide) allows him to find the soft spots in zone coverage. Taking the primetime stage at Estadio Azteca against a creative, blitz-heavy Minnesota defense, Kittle's blocking prowess keeps him on the field nearly every offensive snap, setting up lethal play-action shots down the seam. Never bench Kittle out of matchup fear. His red-zone involvement and explosive ceiling are far too valuable. Colston Loveland: A Rising Fantasy Option Week 11 Matchup: Chicago Bears vs. New Orleans Saints (Sunday, 12:00 PM CST) Oct 22, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland (84) takes the field prior to the game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field. Returning to Soldier Field to face the Saints, Loveland's smooth route-running and catch radius gives his quarterback an inviting target between the hashes and in the end zone. Tier 3: Matchup-Based Starters & Sleepers Mike Gesicki: A Matchup Worth Exploiting Week 11 Matchup: Cincinnati Bengals vs. Washington Commanders (Monday, 7:15 PM CST) Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki (88) catches a pass and turns down field for a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 8 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. The Bengals played to a 43-36 overtime win against the Titans. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect If you are streaming the position or dealing with injuries, Gesicki headlines the Week 11 waiver-wire and matchup plays. Wrapping up the slate on Monday Night Football against a Washington defense that has consistently struggled to contain opposing tight ends, Gesicki's slot-heavy deployment essentially turns him into a big-bodied wide receiver. In PPR formats, his favorable coverage matchups and red-zone size makes him an ideal plug-and-play streamer. With opposing defensive coordinators having to deal with stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, Gesicki should get plenty of looks in single coverage. Dalton Kincaid: A Solid-Receiving Option Week 11 Matchup: Buffalo Bills vs. Miami Dolphins (Sunday, 12:00 PM CST) Nov 1, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid (86) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kincaid's usage has fluctuated at times, yet his talent as a natural separator in the middle of the field remains undeniable whenever Buffalo leans into its passing game. Facing AFC East rival Miami in a divisional clash with shootout potential, Kincaid projects to see steady chain-moving looks underneath while defenses account for Buffalo's perimeter speed. He profiles as a dependable PPR floor play with the upside to find the end zone. item.title: New York Yankees Dealt Good News on Top Free Agent Target
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 24: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates hits an RBI single in the first inning during the game against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 24, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 23: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates watches his hit go for a solo home run during the second inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) Getty Major League Baseball’s hot stove season is finally here, and it’s expected to heat up this week, with a number of roster deadlines on the horizon. The New York Yankees are expected to be as active as ever, and the organization got some good news on Tuesday (11/17) (MLB’s QO deadline) when 2B Brandon Lowe declined the Pirates’ Qualifying Offer, immediately making him a free agent. The Yankees are thought to have checked in on Lowe, as the power-hitting 2B is perhaps the biggest infielder on the market (along with Jazz Chisholm Jr.). More MLB on Heavy: New York Mets Quietly Trade 23-Year-Old Pitcher to Rangers Yankees Can Now Officially Pursue Brandon Lowe Getty PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 23: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates watches his hit go for a solo home run during the second inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) It was definitely expected that Brandon Lowe would decline the Qualifying Offer, especially after the 2026 campaign he had from an offensive perspective. CBSSports.com’s RotoWire staff wrote (about Lowe): “Lowe was acquired via trade from the Rays last winter and went on to slash .260/.331/.493 with 35 home runs, 96 RBI and a career-high plus-15 Outs Above Average at second base. The Pirates are interested in bringing Lowe back, but they will have stiff competition and Pittsburgh rarely wins a bidding war. If Lowe signs elsewhere for at least $50 million, the Pirates will receive a draft pick as compensation.” Lowe will likely sign for $50+ million. And with the Yankees not expected to bring back Chisholm Jr., Lowe stands out as an ideal infield free agent target for New York, but the Pirates will also be among the suitors across MLB in attempts to acquire his services for 2027 and beyond. More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Trade Idea Lands $70 Million All-Star Infielder to Replace Ha-Seong Kim Why Brandon Lowe is a Good Fit in New York While New York Yankees fans may say that the team needs to add more right-handed hitters, considering Brandon Lowe came off a 2026 season where he hit 35 home runs, there’s no telling how his left-handed stroke will play in the Bronx, which could only result in more longballs and extra-base hits. Plus, the Yankees are pretty familiar with Lowe’s ability from his time in the AL East with the Rays. Expect a lot of reports in the coming day

item.title: No. 8 UH cruises past Rutgers at Players Era 8 to stay unbeaten on season
item.description: UH's Arafan Diané (13) celebrates with teammates during the first half of Tuesday's win over Rutgers at the the Players Era 8 in Las Vegas. (Zach Del Bello via Players Era/Getty Images) LAS VEGAS - Dedan Thomas Jr. had 21 points, and the University of Houston jumped out to a big first-half lead to beat Rutgers 85-73 on Tuesday in the first game at the Players Era 8. Mercy Miller added 15 points, answering with a layup and free throw after the Scarlet Knights had cut a 21-point deficit to nine with about 13 minutes remaining. Rutgers (3-1) got within eight points, 69-61, on a spin move by Christian Gurdak with 6:17 left but couldn't get any closer. Chase McCarty added 12 points for the Cougars, who have won 44 straight regular-season games against unranked opponents. UH (4-0) advanced to Wednesday's 3:30 p.m. CT semifinals against the winner between No. 1 Florida and Notre Dame winner, who play later Tuesday afternoon. The Cougars played most of the second half without JoJo Tugler, who was in foul trouble and finished with four points and seven rebounds. The two teams were called for a combined 59 fouls during the game. Chendall Weaver added 11 points and six rebounds off the bench for the Cougars, who overcame two lengthy scoring droughts in the second half. Delrecco Gillespie had 11 points and six rebounds. item.title: Dolphins lose promising young defender to season-ending injury
item.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images. Dolphins lose promising young defender to season-ending injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As if the Miami Dolphins season couldn’t get any worse, Fins fans will now have to watch the second half of the 2026 season without one of their more promising players making weekly progress on the defensive side of the ball: Jordan Phillips . One of the more encouraging young players on the defensive side of the ball, Phillips will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after suffering a torn biceps in Week 10 against the Indianapolis Colts, according to ESPN Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques. “Per source, Dolphins DT Jordan Phillips will miss the remainder of the season with torn biceps he suffered in the team’s loss to the Colts in Week 10,” Louis-Jacques wrote. “The 2025 fifth-round pick played 60% of the Dolphins’ defensive snaps this season and was poised for an ever larger role after the injury to Zach Sieler. A brutal update for Miami, which has now lost three defensive tackles to season-ending injuries in the past two weeks.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Initially drafted in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft out of Maryland, Phillips has found a home in Sean Duggan’s defense as an athletic nose tackle, amassing 28 tackles, 1 tackle for loss, and two QB hits over 327 defensive snaps . While it would have been interesting to see how Phillips continued to grow down the stretch in Year 2, especially with Sieler also injured , the collegiate Terrapin has proven he can be a legitimate defensive contributor at the NFL level and will be ready to go in 2027 when the Dolphins can hopefully take a step forward as a program. item.title: Magic End 1,429-Day TD Garden Winless Streak With Physical Play
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics got a wake-up call on Monday night. The Orlando Magic ended a winless run at TD Garden that lasted 1,429 days. This is not just a bad loss; it is a statement made by a team that refused to back down. The Magic took down the top-seeded Celtics with a final score of 115-105. That streak of losses inside the Garden has been broken after nearly four full calendar years. A Physical Statement The game did not start well for Boston. The Magic opened the night with a cold shooting start, making only 4 of 18 shots in the first 9:50. They managed just 12 points during that slow stretch. But the story changed quickly. The Orlando Magic made their final three shots of the quarter. They held Boston to just 17 points, the fewest the Celtics have scored in any quarter so far this season. Boston could not find a rhythm. In the opening half, the Celtics managed only a 34.6 percent shooting rate. They made only 7 of 27 shots from deep. Throughout most of the season, the Magic’s defense had not appeared as physical as it did. This shift in tone forced Boston into tough looks and low-percentage attempts. The Celtics’ six-game win streak ended because they could not handle the contact. Bitadze Makes His Mark Orlando found a key weapon in their frontcourt. Goga Bitadze served as a vertical spacer for the Magic in the second consecutive game. In 20 minutes of play, the 7-footer scored 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting. His efficiency was vital to the team’s success. Over the last two games, Bitadze is now 10-for-11 from the field. He has also grabbed 10 combined rebounds in that span. This win marks the Magic’s fourth-straight victory. It is easily their biggest win to date. The numbers show a team that has figured out how to win on the road. The Celtics must now deal with a Magic squad that plays with renewed confidence.

item.title: Arch Manning Leads Texas Past LSU Despite Three Interceptions
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Arch Manning threw three interceptions on Saturday night and still found a way to beat LSU 22-21 in Baton Rouge. This result keeps the Longhorns in the playoff hunt while knocking the Tigers out of the race. The win proves that a flawed team can still make a deep run if it gets the job done when the clock winds down. According to ESPN , Manning threw one touchdown on 19 completions out of 35 passes for 174 yards. Those numbers look bad on paper. Yet he made the one play that changed the game. He found Raleek Brown for a four-yard score with three seconds left. That strike secured the victory and cemented Texas’ place in the conversation for the next two weeks. The Manning Legacy Lives On Arch Manning grew up watching games at this very stadium. He pointed out his old seats to his teammates before the final drive. The win feels personal for a quarterback who has family ties to the venue. His grandfather Archie led comebacks at Tiger Stadium. Now Arch has joined that list of legends. “That’s what it’s all about: Death Valley at night, two-minute drive, let’s go,” Manning said. The quote captures the drama of the moment perfectly. He also called the win a memory he will keep for the rest of his life. It was a tough night for the defense, but the offense delivered when it mattered most. SEC Power Shifts Again The SEC might still get two first-round byes this year. Kentucky’s loss to Florida opens the door for other teams like Wake Forest, Iowa, or Oregon to move up. The conference could end up with only four teams in the top 12 on Tuesday night. Heather Dinich reported for ESPN that the committee is very high on Georgia. The Bulldogs dismantled Missouri on Saturday and jumped out to a 31-7 halftime lead. Their strong analytics and complete team play should keep them at the top. Meanwhile, Texas just needs to keep winning to stay in the mix. The Longhorns are not perfect, but they know how to close out games. Arch Manning threw three picks yet still led the final drive from the 42-yard line. He converted three third downs to set up the winning score. Texas now sits at 8-2. The team faces two more games before the final rankings drop.

item.title: Kelce Clears Ankle Scare, Backs Chiefs’ Snap Decision
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs secured a dominant 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, but the win brought a fresh worry for fans. Star tight end Travis Kelce left the field early with a limp after a hard tackle in the first quarter. He returned before halftime, yet his playing time dropped significantly for the rest of the game. Kelce addressed the situation after the final whistle, explaining that the team made the call to limit his snaps. Speaking to USA Today, Kelce said, according to Yahoo Sports , “I’m all good. I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them.” He noted that younger players stepped up well, adding, “It was really nice” to see so many young guys step up. The 37-year-old had entered the game with existing ankle issues, a detail former NFL doctor David Chao highlighted. The Hit and The History The injury occurred just minutes into the game when Kelce caught a 23-yard pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Video evidence shows Kelce heading straight to the locker room for his left ankle after the play. This moment felt different from a similar scare in Week 6 against the Chargers, where he played through the pain. Sunday looked messier, with fans furious over a tackle by Falcons defender DeMarcco Hellams that appeared to twist Kelce’s ankle awkwardly. Despite the pain, Kelce kept making history, having recently set the all-time record for career yards after the catch. While Kelce dealt with the injury, Mahomes put the team on his back with a massive performance. The quarterback finished with 348 passing yards and five touchdowns, his best statistical output in over four years. The Chiefs improved to a 7-2 record on the season, silencing doubts about their offense reaching previous highs. A Tough Road Ahead The team now faces a critical stretch of games with Kelce’s health in question. His fellow tight end, Jared Wiley, was also ruled out with a right ankle injury, leaving the roster thin. The Chiefs have a week to prepare for their next matchup. The team will host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Arrowhead Stadium. The offense loses its most trusted target if Kelce cannot go. Despite the scare, Kelce remains confident about his recovery. He told reporters that there were many questions about the team early in the season, but they have found answers. “There were a lot of questions, wasn’t there?” he said. “We got some answers.” The Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13, but the win does not erase the worry about Kelce’s body handling the weekly grind at age 37.

His fellow tight end, Jared Wiley, was also ruled out with a right ankle injury, leaving the roster thin. The Chiefs have a week to prepare for their next matchup. The team will host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Arrowhead Stadium. The offense loses its most trusted target if Kelce cannot go. Despite the scare, Kelce remains confident about his recovery. He told reporters that there were many questions about the team early in the season, but they have found answers. “There were a lot of questions, wasn’t there?” he said. “We got some answers.” The Chiefs beat the Falcons 35-13, but the win does not erase the worry about Kelce’s body handling the weekly grind at age 37.

item.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
item.description: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese football federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. Turn a new page and all that. This was a welcome victory for Jorge Jesus, for whom a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark a few days ago was a harrowing juncture, and there were plenty of positive takeaways for Wales, too. David Brooks cancelled out Bruno Fernandes’s opener from the edge of the box and then seized the lead through Sorba Thomas, who applied the finishing touch to a purring team move. But Neto, who picked up two bookings in one minute and 59 seconds, the second for a foul on Brennan Johnson, equalised before half-time. Craig Bellamy’s side were fun and, at times, freewheeling but Forbs had the final say with a neat run and finish. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
item.description: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 43-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4m) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the English players’ union observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money. Continue reading...

item.title: Sloppy Socceroos given a reality check as Jordan dominate in friendly win
item.description: Jordan 2-0 Australia (Al-Taamari 34, Ali Olwan 90+3) Socceroos had just one effort on target in defeat In their final game of 2026, the Socceroos were given a reminder that they remain a work in progress, beaten 2-0 by Jordan in an international friendly where the scoreline failed to reflect the first-half siege the victors laid on their opponent’s goal, nor the unforced errors and brain fades that helped doom the Australians’ hopes of firing a shot in response. Optimism was high for those in green and gold after their comfortable win against the reigning Asian champions Qatar on Friday but very quickly on Tuesday it was made apparent that the Jordanians were to provide far more spirited opposition. This time around it would be the Australians that were to be the subject of a first-half onslaught, as a Jordan team inspired by Musa al-Taamari launched forward with wicked pace and ruthless intent whenever the opportunity, or space left by the Socceroo defence, presented itself. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly obituary
item.description: Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football. In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur. Continue reading...

item.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
item.description: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Jürgen Klopp hard-launches his Germany rebuilding project in style
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Barely six weeks ago, Jürgen Klopp’s big home debut in the Germany dugout ended in a deeply frustrating 1-0 Nations League defeat to Greece – but the manager tasked with returning Die Mannschaft to relevance claimed not to care. “I’m completely unbothered,” Klopp trilled unconvincingly. “I’ve lost far more matches than I would have liked, but as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately a piece of information – no different from a win.” It was a quote straight out of the Pierre Sage playbook for unfussed continental coaches – and probably worried a few German FA suits, given Klopp had already threatened to quit at his own unveiling over potential media intrusion and criticism. “If you say tomorrow, ‘he’s [sh!t]’, tell me to my face and I’m out,” Klopp roared to trembling hacks in July . That imagined confrontation now looks unlikely to take place, because his Germany side are suddenly very good indeed. Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
item.description: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling. Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days , Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer . He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records. Continue reading...

item.title: Declan Rice agrees new Arsenal contract making him club’s joint highest-paid player
item.description: Deal will run to 2031 and worth about £300,000 a week Jurriën Timber also agrees fresh contract extension Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year contract at Arsenal, with the England midfielder poised to match Bukayo Saka’s status as the highest-paid player at the Premier League champions. Representatives for Rice, who won his 82nd cap in England’s thrilling win over Spain on Sunday, have been in talks for months about extending the deal he signed in 2023 after a record £105m move from West Ham. That is believed to be worth about £250,000 a week and is due to expire in 2028, although Arsenal have the option of a further 12 months. Continue reading...

item.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
item.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2 . The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before. The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

item.title: Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion
item.description: Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action. Fifa is a signatory to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”. They can have their status as a signatory removed, however, if “sincerity in participation or ability to participate is a cause for concern”. Continue reading...

item.title: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
item.description: As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike. So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson. Continue reading...

item.title: Switzerland roll over sorry Scotland to increase the pressure on Pocognoli
item.description: A match that should have been about 103 was instead about four. Andy Robertson is due acclaim for becoming the most capped player in Scotland’s history but how the full-back will wish the moment had arrived in different circumstances. A second-string Switzerland team pulled Scotland apart, raising further and significant questions about the suitability of Sébastien Pocognoli to carry out the job his paymasters boldly entrusted him with. Scottish FA giddiness about Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke, a hugely successful leader of the national team, is looking increasingly ridiculous. “I don’t think you’ve got time in international football,” said Robertson as dust settled here. Ouch. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Have a question for Jonathan? Email soccerwithjw@theguardian.com , and he’ll answer the best in a future edition. Continue reading...

item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne Wrack Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...

item.title: European football body’s plan to go global leaves Fifa on tenterhooks
item.description: Findings of ‘feasibility study’ into quest for world domination loom with Europe’s wealthiest certain to benefit whatever the outcome It will be one of the most eagerly devoured documents in football circles, assuming its contents are ever fully revealed. In September, the increasingly powerful European Football Clubs body announced a “feasibility study” into how it can become established on a more global scale, morphing into an organisation that represents clubs all over the world. The study’s findings could, some leading figures in the sport’s governance believe, define football’s long-term future. It has the potential to transform a landscape destabilised by the scandals surrounding Fifa and Gianni Infantino . Continue reading...

item.title: Three Lions’ win over Spain comes in two acts: the first superb, the second heroic | Sid Lowe
item.description: Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding In the final, absurdly tense moments before England finally did it and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: s omehow, anyhow . What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too. Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch. Continue reading...

item.title: Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain
item.description: As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watched Kenny Dalglish only on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Dalglish’s international career ended at 102 and the curious events that meant he missed the 1986 World Cup. There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier. Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport. Instead, Robertson’s march to the top of the cap pile gives cause to laud his contribution. Continue reading...

item.title: Terry Butcher: ‘I’ve learned to live with the Hand of God goal better’
item.description: The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places “Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona. Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”? Butcher found himself in the post-match doping-control room alongside his nemesis at the Azteca in 1986. “I tapped my head, then my hand, and then he tapped his head,” Butcher says. “He didn’t admit to it because, if he had, I’d have been right across that room.” Continue reading...

item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.title: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson
item.description: Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013 For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and caused his sacking , consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one. The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. Except Wilcox disagreed and Sir Jim Ratcliffe went with Wilcox’s man, Ruben Amorim, and that December Ashworth departed only five months after joining. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Pregnancy does not mean game over’: meet the footballers challenging the myths | Moving the Goalposts
item.description: Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to run at 81% of her max speed at 32 weeks pregnant. Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for Angel City FC , documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, Millie Bright announced her pregnancy in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal. Continue reading...

item.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. Continue reading...

item.title: Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number
item.description: Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure. *** Continue reading...

item.title: Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate
item.description: Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his career It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.” Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Tullis-Joyce takes charge and is Shaw the perfect striker?
item.description: The City forward hit a WSL hat-trick for the ninth time while Eva Olid’s United have found defensive stability Not only did Khadija “Bunny” Shaw score a record-extending ninth WSL hat-trick, she scored a “perfect hat-trick” for the fourth time in the competition, something nobody else has managed more than once. Against West Ham the Jamaica striker opened the scoring with her left foot, headed home her second off the underside of the crossbar and tucked in her third with her right foot late on. It helped her side towards a 5-0 win that opened up a two-point gap at the top of the table and stretched Shaw’s lead in the race to be the top division’s top scorer to a five-goal advantage over her nearest challenger, Océane Hurtré. Can anybody stop her relentless pursuit of another Golden Boot? It would appear not. Tom Garry Match report: Liverpool 1-2 Arsenal Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. Jonathan Wilson Match report: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City Match report: Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa Match report: Brighton 2-0 Brentford Match report: Arsenal 1-0 Hull Match report: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea Match report: Leeds 1-0 Tottenham Continue reading...

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap . Living in Australia? Try the Guardian Australia’s daily sports newsletter Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Recap newsletter: our free sport highlights email
item.description: The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Subscribe to get our editors’ pick of the Guardian’s award-winning sport coverage. We’ll email you the stand-out features and interviews, insightful analysis and highlights from the archive, plus films, podcasts, galleries and more – all arriving in your inbox at every Friday lunchtime. And we’ll set you up for the weekend and let you know our live coverage plans so you’ll be ahead of the game. Here’s what you can expect from us.
